foot.later: You can change it any time in Settings → Access & safety.

access.title: Who can open Claudio

intro.none: Right now anyone who reaches this port can use it. If Claudio runs on a server or on a network, ask for a token.
intro.token: Every request has to carry the token. Keep it that way if Claudio runs on a server or on a network.
intro.oidc: Every request has to carry a sign-in from your identity provider (OIDC).

access.introPhone: If it runs on a server or on a network, ask for a token.
access.body: Every request has to carry the token. With “None”, anyone who reaches the port can use Claudio: fine on your own computer, not on a network.
access.oidc: OIDC is on. You change it in Settings → Access & safety.
access.more: OIDC and the read-only mode are in Settings → Access & safety.
access.shownOnceBody: It is shown only this once. This browser already uses it; anything else that calls the API will need it.
access.readOnly: Claudio is in read-only mode: the access cannot be changed from here.

remote.name: Tailscale
remote.meta: Reach Claudio from your phone, on your tailnet

reason.signedIn: Signed in. You open the tunnel in Settings → Access & safety → Remote access, once the access above asks for a token.
reason.loggedOut: Not signed in to a tailnet yet. Sign in with a link or an auth key.
reason.stopped: Signed in, but not connected. Sign in again to connect it.
reason.daemonDown: The Tailscale service of this container is not answering. Restart the container.
reason.machine: Tailscale on this machine is yours to sign in, with its app or tailscale up. Claudio uses it as it is.
reason.missing: Tailscale is not installed on this machine.

agents.title: Sign in to your agents
agents.intro: Each agent uses its own account. Sign in here, with a code or a key: there is no need to open a terminal on the server.
agents.introPhone: With a code or a key, without opening a terminal on the server.

code.title: Connect your code and your work items
code.intro: GitHub and GitLab for your projects' PRs and MRs; YouTrack to bring in its issues. All of it is optional.
code.introPhone: GitHub and GitLab for PRs and MRs; YouTrack for its issues. All of it is optional.

done.title: Claudio is ready
done.intro: This is what got done. What you skipped is still in Settings, in the same panel you saw here, and this assistant does not come back.
done.introPhone: What you skipped is still in Settings, in the same panel.

panel.title: Sign in to {{label}}

link.tailscale: Create an auth key in the Tailscale admin console

hint.envSealed: Kept encrypted, and only {{label}}'s processes receive it. It is not shown again.
hint.envPlain: Kept in a file only the server's user can read, and only {{label}}'s processes receive it. It is not shown again.
hint.gh: With the repo, read:org and workflow scopes. gh keeps it in its own configuration; Claudio keeps no copy.
hint.glab: With the api and write_repository scopes. glab keeps it in its own configuration; Claudio keeps no copy.
hint.tailscale: One use is enough: Tailscale keeps this machine signed in with a key of its own, and Claudio keeps no copy. It reaches Tailscale through a file only it can read, removed right after.

panel.claude: Claude Code has no sign-in Claudio can do for you. On your own computer, where you already use Claude, run claude setup-token in a terminal: it opens the browser, you sign in with your subscription, and it shows you a token that lasts a year. Paste it here.
panel.claudeApiKey: An Anthropic API key bills the API account it belongs to, not your subscription.
panel.viaNote: {{label}} uses your {{via}} sign-in ({{cli}}). This code signs {{cli}} in to {{host}}, and {{label}} works with it from then on.
panel.open: Open this page on any device:
panel.type: Type this code and approve the access.
panel.openLink: Open this link on any device where you can sign in to Tailscale:
panel.approveLink: Sign in and connect this machine to your tailnet. There is no code to type.

fail.cli-refused: {{label}} refused the sign-in. If it was a key, check it is right and has not expired.
fail.not-signed-in: The command finished, but {{label}} is still signed out.
fail.no-code: {{label}} finished without showing a code. Try a key.
fail.cli-missing: {{label}}'s program is not on this machine.
fail.timeout: {{label}} did not answer in time and Claudio stopped it.
fail.expired: The code expired: nobody approved it within 15 minutes.

signOut.title: Sign out of {{label}}?
signOut.body: Claudio stops using {{label}} until someone signs in again, and its chats that are running may fail.
signOut.bodyKey: Claudio forgets the key it keeps for {{label}}. If {{label}} has no other sign-in, it stops working and its running chats may fail.
signOut.bodyHost: {{cli}} forgets its sign-in to {{host}}. Claudio cannot read or merge the PRs or MRs there until someone signs in again.
signOut.unsupported: {{label}} documents no way to sign out from a program.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.body: The agents' keys, YouTrack's token and what you paste when you sign in are kept encrypted in <mono>secrets.json</mono>, and each one reaches only its own tool's processes. They are never shown, in a log or in an answer of the API.
secrets.bodyPlain: The agents' keys, YouTrack's token and what you paste when you sign in are kept in <mono>secrets.json</mono>, which only the server's user can read, and each one reaches only its own tool's processes. They are never shown, in a log or in an answer of the API.
secrets.besideTitle: The key is next to the data
secrets.besideBody: Claudio made it in its data folder (<mono>secret.key</mono>) because it was given none. It protects a copy of the files, such as a backup, but not the volume: whoever reads the volume has both.
secrets.recommend: Recommended: pass the key in the <mono>CLAUDIO_SECRET_KEY</mono> environment variable and keep it outside the volume.
secrets.plainBody: There is no key (a desktop app without a keyring, or an install from source), so values are kept as they are, in a file with 0600 permissions. Pass a key in <mono>CLAUDIO_SECRET_KEY</mono> to encrypt them.
secrets.setupTitle: The keys you save are encrypted, but the key is next to the data
secrets.setupBody: It protects a copy of the files, not the volume. Pass the key in <mono>CLAUDIO_SECRET_KEY</mono> so it lives outside it.
